record.original_question: Let Bd be the parameter space of holomorphic foliations of degree d ≥ 2 and let Bc_d be the subset consisting of foliations that admit directed positive closed currents. Is Bc_d a countable union of proper analytic subsets of Bd?

evidence.quote: Let Bcd denote the set of foliations which admit directed positive closed currents. It is clearly a closed set in Bd.
Problem 3.3. Is the space Bcd a countable union of proper analytic subsets of Bd, when d ≥ 2 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\geq 2$, let $\mathcal{B}_d$ denote the parameter space of singular holomorphic foliations by Riemann surfaces of degree $d$ in the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ (equivalently, the Zariski-open subset of $\mathbb{P}^N$, for the appropriate $N=N(d)$, parametrizing foliations whose singular set is finite). A positive closed current $T$ of bidimension $(1,1)$ on $\mathbb{P}^2$ is said to be directed by a foliation $\mathcal{F}\in\mathcal{B}_d$ if, on every flow box of $\mathcal{F}$ outside the singular set, $T$ is locally a superposition of integration currents along the local leaves. Let
$$\mathcal{B}^c_d := \{\mathcal{F}\in\mathcal{B}_d : \mathcal{F}\text{ admits a non-zero directed positive closed current}\}.$$
It is known that $\mathcal{B}^c_d$ is a closed subset of $\mathcal{B}_d$. Determine whether $\mathcal{B}^c_d$ is a countable union of proper analytic subsets of $\mathcal{B}_d$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any later work explicitly resolving whether the locus of degree-$d$ holomorphic foliations in $\mathbb{P}^2$ admitting a directed positive closed current is a countable union of proper analytic subsets of the parameter space. Related results show that foliations with only hyperbolic singularities and no invariant algebraic curve admit no directed positive closed current (and form the complement of a countable union of proper analytic subsets), but the precise structural question for $\mathcal{B}^c_d$ does not appear to be settled in the sources found.
